study.design: prospective observational cohort (active surveillance of invasive candidiasis in a NICU)

study.comments: 4 C. tropicalis cases (7%), only 3 tested for MIC. One C. tropicalis isolate was resistant to fluconazole (MIC >128) and itraconazole; the text says itraconazole MIC >64 µg/mL, but Table 2 gives an MIC range up to >32 (>64 is the MFC). The itraconazole MIC50 of 1.03 suggests a second isolate with MIC around 1 µg/mL (R by current CLSI), but the authors report only one non-susceptible isolate. n_candida_total = 58 Candida cases (59 neonates; 58 cases across species in Fig. 2). Very small n.

The resistance rows for the subset use the individual MICs. The subset is biased (resistant isolates only).

clade4.evidence: Molecularly, FNS isolates were characterized by ERG11 Y132F ± S154F, a recurrent UPC2 Q289L substitution, up-regulation of efflux pump genes (CDR1, CDR2, and MDR1), and predominance of DST538/DST544 lineages.
clade4.note: The authors associate DST544/DST538 (CC10) with fluconazole resistance but do not call them 'clade 4' and caution against inferring clonality from MLST. Equivalence with clade 4 is not established in the article. The references cite the azole-resistant genotype from orchards.

dynamics.description: Annual FNS among sterile-site isolates fluctuated between 3.8% and 12.5% (mean 8.2%) with no linear trend (OR per year 1.12, 95% CI 0.90-1.41; P=0.31)
